goals.title: Ship a working incident tracker
goals.body: Build an on-call incident tracker from vague stakeholder requirements. Teams report production incidents, responders acknowledge and resolve them, and leadership needs a read-only status view. Support severity levels, assignment, status lifecycle, comments/timeline, search, REST API, responder/admin dashboard, public status page, audit log, and authentication. Technology stack is not prescribed — the agent decides.

tasks.title: Design system architecture and data model
tasks.body: Choose stack (language, framework, DB). Design schema: incidents, users/roles, severity, status machine, assignment, comments/timeline, audit events. Define REST API surface. Produce SPEC.md and PLANNING-MATRIX.md before implementation.

tasks.title: Implement REST API and auth
tasks.body: Build backend API: login/session, incident CRUD, status transitions, assignment, comments, search/filter. Enforce role-based access (reporter, responder, admin). All routes must have tests.

tasks.title: Implement responder/admin dashboard
tasks.body: Browser UI for responders and admins: incident list with filters, detail view, assign/unassign, status updates, add comments, audit trail visible. Must work against the live API.

tasks.title: Implement public status page
tasks.body: Minimal read-only public page: summary of active/open incidents (title, severity, status, started time). No auth for visitors. Must reflect live API data.

tasks.title: End-to-end verification
tasks.body: Run full test suite. Manually verify reporter create, responder acknowledge/assign/resolve, public status view, admin audit. Document in VERIFY.md.

assumptions.title: Stack is agent choice
assumptions.body: No technology stack is prescribed. The agent chooses language, framework, and database.

assumptions.title: Public status page is read-only
assumptions.body: The public page displays active incident summary only — no visitor login or write actions.

assumptions.title: At least three severity levels required
assumptions.body: Incidents must support at minimum three distinct severity levels (e.g. P1/P2/P3 or critical/high/medium).
